thread:
ops-bot: ALERT: realtime p99 spike detected for /v1/generate (hosted-eu). p99 = 2.8s (baseline ~0.6s), p95 = 0.9s. Alert id: alert/rt-latency-eu-2087. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rt-latency?orgId=1&panelId=7&var-region=eu

alex: Ack. I'm oncall — paging SREs and starting triage. First quick checks: health endpoints, rollout status, and any recent deploys.

maya: Noted. I'm already seeing streaming stalls metric jump: stream_stalls_total rate +120% over last 5m. Most of the increase is for chunked (streaming) responses routed through proxy-eu-2.

raj: Any deploys in the last hour? I see a canary for model-serving-service pushed ~00:42 UTC to eu clusters (canary id: canary-9082). Could be related.

luis: I pushed a small serving runtime kernel tweak yesterday to improve batching. It was targeted at dedicated pools, but double-checking now whether the change propagated to any hosted shards by mistake.

alex: Quick mitigation plan so we don't page customers:
- Step A: Disable streaming for the slow route (turn chunked->polling fallback)
- Step B: Route new requests on /v1/generate to fallback model rdx-small-quantized for eu region
- Step C: Increase serving pool replicas for hosted-eu by +2 (temporary)
- Step D: If p99 remains > SLO, roll back canary canary-9082

alex: Running health check against a sampled token path now:
```
curl -s -X POST https://hosted-eu.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rdx-large","input":"hello","stream":true}' -o /tmp/resp.txt -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
cat /tmp/resp.txt | tail -n 10
```

incident-bot: Incident INC-5123 created: Realtime p99 latency spike (hosted-eu). Priority: P1 (potential customer impact). Pager: SRE oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-5123

oncall-sre: taking this. coordinating with infra to provision extra capacity now. Posting to #support to warn CS/ops. I'll also set a canary rollback hold until we confirm.

maya: Customer impact check: top affected customers by error rate (last 15m):
```
topk(10, sum by (customer) (increase(stream_errors_total[15m])))
```
Result: 12 customers > 5% error increase, estimated 2.4% of total requests in eu affected. Most are heavy streaming customers.

raj: Logs from frontend proxy show repeated 502/503s with message 'upstream response timeout' and increased queue depth on proxy-eu-2. Also seeing a spike in kv-cache miss latency which correlates with tail tokens.

luis: If kv cache misses spike, that increases decode time. We can try a targeted cache flush for low-value prefixes to drop hot-set pressure. Admin API (example):
```
POST https://admin.hosted-eu.redwood.internal/cache/flush
{"prefix":"user:prefix:temp-", "shards":["proxy-eu-2"]}
```
I can run that after we validate it won't evict useful entries.

alex: I'm flipping traffic for /v1/generate -> fallback model rdx-small-quantized for eu region now (canary traffic 100% -> fallback). Applying route change...

alex: Route change applied. Starting immediate scale up of hosted-eu serving pool (replicas +2).

maya: After the route change: p95 dropped to 0.7s (good), p99 improved to ~1.8s (better but still above SLO). stream_stalls reduced by ~45%.

raj: We're still seeing long-tail outliers from a subset of requests that request very long context (>4096 tokens). Those requests disproportionately hit the KV cache and cause backend stall while fetching large KV entries.

alex: Mitigation 2: temporary request shaping — cap tokens/request to 2048 for eu region via routing policy to reduce backpressure. Applying token cap now.

luis: Token cap in place. Also pushed a slow-path throttle on decoder workers so a single long request can't starve others.

maya: Observability note: traces for a sample tail request: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/abc123 — shows a 1.2s wait on redis-prefetch and 0.9s queueing at worker.

incident-bot: INC-5123 update: Mitigations applied: fallback model routing, +2 replicas, token cap. Monitoring p95/p99.

alex: Current status: p95 ~0.7s (within SLO), p99 ~1.4s (still above target 500ms). Customer impact reduced but not fully resolved. Preparing an incident summary for status page and support triage.

oncall-sre: Handoff plan: I'll remain for next 30m and then hand off to raj (night SRE). If p99 not back to <=500ms before handoff, escalate to eng-runtime for deep kernel/runtime investigation.

raj: I'll take the handoff. Next steps for me: check model-serving canary logs for memory pressure, run heap and GC stats, and validate there are no hot loops in token fetching. Also coordinate with infra for a temporary capacity bump if we see renewed queue growth.

maya: I'll run a post-mitigation regression check across regions and push a small alert suppression window for noisy p95 alerts while we confirm stability.

alex: TL;DR for status page (draft): "We observed elevated tail latency for realtime generation in EU (p99). Mitigations applied: switched to fallback quantized model, added serving capacity, applied token caps and cache tuning. Impact: partial degradation for streaming customers in EU; now largely mitigated. Engineers continuing follow-up to root cause and rollback verification. Incident: INC-5123."

luis: I'll schedule a follow-up to test KV cache eviction policy and add telemetry slices for token-length vs latency.

incident-bot: INC-5123 annotated: severity=P1, impact=partial, links=[https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rt-latency?orgId=1, https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-5123].

alex: Closing comments: keep alerts at reduced sensitivity for 1 hour; if p99 resurges we re-open and escalate. Handing to raj in 27m. Good triage everyone :thumbsup:
